title: Emergency fund: how much you need, and where to keep it #shorts
description:
A common guideline is 3 to 6 months of essential expenses. With $3,000 a month of essentials, that's $9,000 to $18,000. Keep it somewhere safe and easy to reach, like a high-yield savings account at an FDIC-insured bank, not in the stock market, which can fall right when you need the cash.

Example: $3,000 a month of essentials (rent, food, bills, insurance, transport). Sources: FDIC standard deposit insurance is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category (fdic.gov). The S&P 500 fell about 34% from its 19 Feb 2020 close to its 23 Mar 2020 close (S&P Dow Jones Indices). Savings rates change often; check the current rate before opening an account. Not financial advice.

#emergencyfund #personalfinance #savings #moneytips #budgeting

scenes.say: If your paycheck stopped tomorrow, how many months could you last?
The common guideline: keep three to six months of essential expenses. Rent, food, bills, insurance, getting to work.
If your essentials cost three thousand dollars a month, that's nine thousand to eighteen thousand dollars.
Where should it live? Not in the stock market. In early twenty twenty, US stocks fell about a third in about a month, just as millions lost their jobs.
Keep it in a high-yield savings account at an FDIC-insured bank. Deposits are covered up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars, per depositor, per bank.
It earns some interest, and you can move it to checking in a day or two.
Starting from zero? Aim for one month first. Then build.
Follow for one money lesson every day.
